title: Ensure /tmp is configured on a separate partition
description: The /tmp directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary file storage. Ensure it is mounted as a separate partition with appropriate mount options to restrict execution and device creation.
rationale: Since /tmp is world-writable, making it a separate partition prevents it from being used to fill the root filesystem. Mounting with nodev, nosuid, and noexec prevents creation of device files, setuid binaries, and execution of malicious scripts.
check_content:
Run: findmnt -n /tmp | grep -E 'nodev|nosuid|noexec'
Verify /tmp is mounted with nodev, nosuid, and noexec options.
Also check /etc/fstab for a dedicated /tmp entry.
fix_text:
Add or modify the /tmp entry in /etc/fstab:
tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0
Then run: mount -o remount /tmp

title: Ensure AIDE is installed and configured for file integrity monitoring
description: AIDE (Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment) creates a database of file hashes to detect unauthorized changes to the filesystem.
rationale: File integrity monitoring detects changes to critical system files that may indicate a compromise. Without it, unauthorized modifications can go unnoticed.
check_content:
Run: dpkg -s aide | grep -i status
Verify AIDE is installed.
Run: cat /etc/cron.d/aide or systemctl status aidecheck to verify regular checks are scheduled.
fix_text:
Install AIDE: apt install aide aide-common
Initialize the database: aideinit
Copy the database: cp /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new /var/lib/aide/aide.db
Schedule regular checks in /etc/cron.d/aide: 0 5 * * * root /usr/bin/aide.wrapper --config /etc/aide/aide.conf --check

title: Ensure permissions on bootloader config are restricted (GRUB)
description: The GRUB bootloader configuration file /boot/grub/grub.cfg should be owned by root and not readable or writable by other users.
rationale: The GRUB configuration may contain sensitive information and must not be modified by unauthorized users. An attacker with write access could insert malicious boot parameters.
check_content:
Run: stat /boot/grub/grub.cfg
Verify Access is 0400 or more restrictive, owner is root, group is root.
fix_text:
Run the following commands:
chown root:root /boot/grub/grub.cfg
chmod og-rwx /boot/grub/grub.cfg

title: Disable IPv6 if not required
description: IPv6 should be disabled on systems that do not require it to reduce the attack surface.
rationale: If IPv6 is not needed, disabling it reduces the attack surface. An unmonitored IPv6 stack can be exploited even when IPv4 is properly secured.
check_content:
Run: sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6
Expected output: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1
Also check /etc/sysctl.conf or /etc/sysctl.d/ for persistence.
fix_text:
Add to /etc/sysctl.conf or /etc/sysctl.d/60-disable-ipv6.conf:
net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1
net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 = 1
Run: sysctl -p

title: Ensure SSH Protocol 2 is enforced
description: SSH Protocol 1 has known cryptographic vulnerabilities. Only SSH Protocol 2 should be permitted.
rationale: SSH Protocol 1 suffers from design flaws including weak cryptography. Restricting to Protocol 2 ensures use of stronger encryption and key exchange algorithms.
check_content:
Run: sshd -T | grep -i protocol
Verify output shows: protocol 2
Also check /etc/ssh/sshd_config for 'Protocol 2'.
fix_text:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and ensure:
Protocol 2
Then restart SSH: systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure SSH root login is disabled
description: Direct root login via SSH should be disabled. Administrators should log in as a regular user and escalate privilege as needed.
rationale: Permitting direct root login increases the risk of brute-force attacks and removes accountability by eliminating the audit trail of user escalation.
check_content:
Run: sshd -T | grep permitrootlogin
Expected: permitrootlogin no
fix_text:
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config:
PermitRootLogin no
Restart SSH: systemctl restart sshd

title: Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512
description: The SHA-512 algorithm provides stronger password hashing compared to MD5 or SHA-1.
rationale: Weak password hashing allows offline dictionary or brute-force attacks. SHA-512 with salting significantly increases the cost of such attacks.
check_content:
Run: grep -E '^\$6' /etc/shadow | head -1
The $6$ prefix indicates SHA-512.
Also verify /etc/pam.d/common-password contains 'sha512'.
fix_text:
Edit /etc/pam.d/common-password and ensure the pam_unix.so line includes sha512:
password [success=1 default=ignore] pam_unix.so obscure sha512
Re-hash existing passwords by having users change their passwords.

title: Ensure auditd is installed and running
description: The auditd daemon provides system call and file access auditing capabilities required for security monitoring and compliance.
rationale: Without auditing, it is difficult to detect unauthorized access or changes to the system. Audit logs are critical for incident response and forensic analysis.
check_content:
Run: dpkg -s auditd | grep -i status
Run: systemctl is-active auditd
Expected: active
fix_text:
Install and enable auditd:
apt install auditd audispd-plugins
systemctl enable auditd
systemctl start auditd

title: Ensure /etc/passwd file permissions are configured
description: /etc/passwd must be owned by root with permissions 644 to prevent unauthorized modification of user account data.
rationale: The /etc/passwd file contains account information for all local users. Incorrect permissions could allow unauthorized modifications that grant elevated privileges.
check_content:
Run: stat /etc/passwd
Verify: Access: (0644/-rw-r--r--), Uid: (0/root), Gid: (0/root)

title: Ensure AppArmor is enabled and enforcing profiles
description: AppArmor provides mandatory access control (MAC) to restrict programs' capabilities. All loaded profiles should be in enforcing mode.
rationale: AppArmor confines processes to only the resources they need, limiting the damage a compromised application can cause. Complain-mode profiles provide no protection.
check_content:
Run: apparmor_status | grep -E 'profiles are in enforce mode'
Verify a nonzero number of profiles are in enforce mode.
Run: systemctl is-active apparmor
fix_text:
Install and enable AppArmor:
apt install apparmor apparmor-profiles apparmor-utils
systemctl enable apparmor
systemctl start apparmor
Set all profiles to enforce: aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/*
